items.title: George Wein — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: Yes you are. Where does that come from?

I don't know. You don't know your own character. My wife Joyce said, "You know" …. She fell in love with me, which she did, thank god … she said, "When I realized that you are always thinking of something to do, that you are never sitting there without thinking of something to do." She respected that. I guess that that's … when I had nothing to do, I was thinking of something to do. That's the entrepreneurial spirit, I guess. I always tell someone, "If you want to be free and you want to have a chance in making…
Well, you persevered and you reopened and then we get to that Fall and you book the Shearing Quintet.
